scores.evidence: Kubernetes doesn't let you change a Deployment's selector labels, so a label mismatch forces a side-by-side cutover
scores.rationale: Claims about Argo CD adoption semantics, OIDC sub claims with job_workflow_ref, ECR immutability, expand/contract migrations and GitHub Actions behavior are all accurate, including the subtle parts the design depends on.

scores.evidence: The bulk of the work is moving 50 live services onto it safely, not building the pipeline
scores.rationale: Correctly interprets the hard problem as migration of 50 live services, is credibly buildable by the assumed team, and every exclusion (PR envs, portal, contract testing) is explicit with a trigger to revisit.

scores.evidence: Each cluster's Argo CD reads only its own config repo. CI holds no cluster credentials.
scores.rationale: Component responsibilities, data ownership (system-of-record table) and trust boundaries are stated and honored consistently everywhere, with no contradictions found across sections.

scores.evidence: Four spikes answer the biggest unknowns... prod rollback ≤ 10 min demonstrated
scores.rationale: The riskiest assumptions (workload adoption, migration hooks, publish identity, service variety) get time-boxed spikes before commitment, exit criteria are measurable, baselines are taken, and validation continues post-launch via drills and metrics.

scores.evidence: this plan is built on stated assumptions (A1–A12 in §5)... Impact if wrong / Validated how
scores.rationale: Every load-bearing assumption is explicit with impact-if-wrong, a validation method and date, and all targets are labeled provisional until the M1 baseline.

scores.evidence: Flow 4: Out-of-order builds... Flow 5: Shared workflow regression... Break-glass (if GitHub is unavailable)
scores.rationale: Covers races, duplicate/idempotent promotion, blast radius of shared components, malicious PRs and CD outages with concrete handling, but flaky-test detection and quarantine — a classic CI trust-eroding failure for 50 services — is absent.

scores.evidence: Platform team owns... On-call is business hours for CI. A prod Argo CD outage is P2, because running services are unaffected.
scores.rationale: Ownership split, runbooks, drilled rollback and rebuild, meaningful alerts and a one-new-tool-per-milestone pacing are all sized to the stated 4-person team.

Dominant cost drivers (CI minutes, people time per service) are estimated with a stated basis, labeled as assumptions, with concrete controls and explicit cost triggers for the build-vs-buy runner decision.

scores.evidence: Reversibility | Revisit if... Point of no return: Jenkins is decommissioned at the end of M4
scores.rationale: Every decision carries a reversibility rating and revisit trigger, hard-to-reverse choices (GitOps shape, chart contract, digest promotion) are validated first via pilot/spikes, and the one point of no return is explicit with a fallback archive.

scores.evidence: Canary releases, ephemeral PR environments, a developer portal and self-hosted runners are deferred.
scores.rationale: Starts with the simplest workable path using existing tools, defers speculative components with explicit triggers, and omits no essential for a 50-service migration.

scores.evidence: T1 on day 1. Week 1, in parallel: T2, T3, T5, T7... Changes plan if > 30% are C
scores.rationale: T1–T17 have concrete done-when criteria, the ordering is justified by dependencies and risk, and each spike states exactly how the plan changes if results disappoint.

checklist.evidence: Spike S1: service inventory... classify A/B/C... Service-specific needs go through declared inputs... or an escape hatch (`pre-build` / `post-test` steps in the caller)
Ring 0 is the pilot (M1). Ring 1 is the 6–8 diverse pilots (M2)... the old and new paths run side by side for each service
Build once, promote the digest... What was tested is what ships... ECR: one repo per service, immutable tags
OIDC only, no stored AWS keys. One IAM role per service... PR builds get no role... PR workflows have no secrets
cosign keyless signing... syft SBOM attestation... Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA and allowlisted... Kyverno `verifyImages` in prod
Migrations are expand/contract only... rolling back means redeploying the previous image, which must still work against the expanded schema
Services are already in prod and are deployed independently (no lockstep releases)... Contract tests are deferred
Shared staging; no PR environments... Fixture services live in a `platform-sandbox` namespace. No production data is needed
Build time comes down through dependency caches, Docker layer cache (`type=gha`) and test splitting where p95 exceeds 20 min
400 runs/day × 10 min × 30 days ≈ 120k minutes/month... about $1–3k/month... ARC as fallback (D11)
Platform team owns... both Argo CD instances... delivery-metrics dashboard (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, time to restore)
`main` is protected and needs 1 code-owner approval from someone other than the author... prod PR history = audit ledger... nightly mirror to S3 with Object Lock

traps.evidence: the old and new paths run side by side for each service... After 2 weeks and ≥ 3 successful prod deploys, delete the legacy job
built once into a container image that never changes and is identified by its digest (a content hash)
It authenticates to AWS with GitHub's OIDC tokens, so there are no stored keys... PR builds get no role
each service's promotion runs in a concurrency group `promote-<service>-<env>`... deployed independently (no lockstep releases)
GitHub Actions with central reusable workflows... GitOps pull with Argo CD... avoids a third new tool in M1

note: An exemplary brownfield CI/CD migration plan — technically precise, risk-sequenced and fully actionable; the only notable gaps are deferred contract testing and no flaky-test handling.
